profile.selection_status: Established-only scientific vocabulary; upstream definitions and synonyms; unresolved mappings retained.
profile.research_question: How do soil phosphorus availability and microbial treatments affect potato phosphorus uptake, growth, and tuber phosphorus composition, and how do food phosphate composition and dietary phosphate exposure affect human health outcomes?
profile.scope_description: Cover the full soil-to-potato-to-food-to-human-health journey focused on phosphorus and phosphate. Include: (1) soil phosphorus chemicals, forms, supply, deficiency, and microbial or PGPR treatments; (2) potato phosphorus uptake, organ transport, root/shoot/tuber growth, agronomic traits, yield, and tissue or tuber phosphorus composition; (3) potato and food phosphate composition, phosphate food additives, and dietary phosphate intake or exposure; and (4) human physiological and health outcomes linked to dietary or serum phosphate exposure (renal, cardiovascular, vascular, bone, or endocrine outcomes). Include hormones, metabolites, and physiological mechanisms only when directly connected to phosphorus or phosphate within this journey. Exclude standalone non-phosphorus mineral findings (such as Na, K, Ca, Mg, Zn, or Fe correlations without phosphorus), standalone gene identity or transcript abundance, laboratory methods, and treatment-selection rationales. Distinguish experimental findings, qualified biological statements, and background from other crops or models. A missing ontology term is a vocabulary gap, not an out-of-scope verdict.
